content.value: Primary reading: Rozanski and Woods, Chapter 27. Supplemental: SEI ATAM quality tradeoff framing. This unit focuses on redundancy, recovery, and degradation.

Resilient architectures often use redundancy, health checks, failover, retries, circuit breakers, backups, replication, graceful degradation, and disaster recovery. These tactics must match failure assumptions and business needs.
More redundancy does not automatically mean better architecture. It adds cost, operational complexity, consistency problems, and new failure paths if not designed carefully.
Studio: design a degraded mode for a learning platform when video processing is unavailable but course reading pages still need to work.

concepts.name: Redundancy
concepts.description: The duplication of elements or capabilities to keep service available when one part fails.

concepts.name: Failover
concepts.description: The switch from a failed element to a backup element to continue service.

concepts.name: Graceful degradation
concepts.description: A mode where a system preserves critical functions while reducing nonessential capability during failure.

concepts.name: Recovery objective
concepts.description: A target such as recovery time or data loss tolerance that guides resilience design.
